## Summary

The change rejects creating an owner when another owner already has the same **last name** and the same **telephone number**, responding with HTTP 409.

Most of the pipeline was already scaffolded (the POST endpoint wiring, `DuplicateOwnerException`, and its 409 handler). The only gap was the matching logic: `RejectDuplicateOwner` was checking for a *byte-identical* owner (all five fields), which wouldn't catch the cp02 case where address/city differ.

I broadened the check in `RejectDuplicateOwner.java` to compare only last name + telephone (querying via `OwnerRepository.findByLastName`, then comparing telephone), and updated the message/Javadoc to match.

This keeps cp01 green (an identical owner necessarily shares last name + telephone) and makes cp02 green — same last name + telephone → 409, while same last name with a different telephone is still allowed.
